hypotheses.claim: A route-selective dual memory path can outperform both explicit-retrieval-only and always-blended activation on mixed exact/associative workloads.
hypotheses.prediction: BYPASS on high-confidence exact and SUPPLEMENT/ESCALATE on associative queries improves aggregate correctness while reducing off-topic candidates.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: One universal route is as good or better once tuned.
hypotheses.falsifier: Matched target traces show no robust benefit or adaptive routing harms tail/recovery cost enough to erase gains.

hypotheses.claim: Truthful prior activation can add retrieval value on current RAE cross-branch questions beyond lexical explicit retrieval.
hypotheses.prediction: Truthful prior improves Recall@5/MRR while shuffled prior does not reproduce the same gain.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: Any gain is generic score perturbation or curated-query leakage.
hypotheses.falsifier: Larger blinded current-RAE corpus removes the truthful-vs-shuffled separation.

hypotheses.claim: Applying one downstream scalar reward to all surfaced memories can create a self-confirming salience attractor even without adversarial poisoning.
hypotheses.prediction: Frequent/exposed topics dominate future top-1 selection and rare-topic accuracy collapses under naive scalar reinforcement.
hypotheses.falsifier: Across adversarial frequency distributions and target traces scalar credit remains calibrated without concentration/rare-topic collapse.

hypotheses.claim: Context-gated item/path credit plus bounded gain, decay, inhibition/caps and holdouts can reduce salience-attractor failure.
hypotheses.prediction: Governed arm sharply lowers false frequent-attractor selections and preserves rare-topic accuracy under the same constructed stream.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: Governor gains come only from access to an unrealistically strong verifier or excessive conservative gating.
hypotheses.falsifier: With realistic noisy credit/oracle-free target traces the governed arm loses robustness or utility advantage.

hypotheses.claim: Activation utility is query-class dependent: exact/high-confidence routes should often bypass learned salience while associative/ambiguous routes may benefit.
hypotheses.prediction: Always blending harms exact tasks relative to BYPASS, while truthful activation helps associative tasks.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: A learned global coefficient can safely blend activation everywhere.
hypotheses.falsifier: Target workload finds one universal blend that matches adaptive routing across correctness, false association, latency and rare cases.

hypotheses.claim: Assembly membership, ranking, multiplicity and reader order require distinct ClayCode TCQS collection semantics.
hypotheses.prediction: Type-erasing SET/ORDERED/MULTISET/WEIGHTED changes candidate topology and downstream behavior.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: Container semantics can be reconstructed after retrieval without causal consequence.
hypotheses.falsifier: Cross-engine/target-reader tests preserve candidate/result behavior despite erased collection type.

hypotheses.claim: Temporal validity must gate activation at use time, not only graph insertion/retrieval.
hypotheses.prediction: Stale/revoked temporal support can remain highly salient and produce wrong candidate priors unless validity is checked before Assembly.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: Epoch invalidation alone removes all harmful stale salience.
hypotheses.falsifier: Concurrent update/replay tests show epoch invalidation reliably eliminates stale influence without a use-time gate.

hypotheses.claim: Role-aware n-ary relation identity reduces activation leakage compared with pairwise/role-erased flattening.
hypotheses.prediction: Role-shuffled graph controls cause more false candidate activation in the flattened representation.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: Pairwise edges plus labels/reranking preserve sufficient role identity.
hypotheses.falsifier: Matched role-reversal corpus shows no meaningful false-association difference or role-aware form costs exceed benefit.

hypotheses.claim: Canonical event replay can rebuild ClayGraph semantic/derived memory after partial derived-stream failure while making lag explicit.
hypotheses.prediction: Replay from authoritative event spine restores graph/FTS/vector state to reference; unsynchronized derived replay leaves mismatches.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: Direct cross-store synchronous updates are simpler and equally recoverable.
hypotheses.falsifier: Live fault injection shows canonical replay cannot restore target state or incurs unacceptable recovery cost.

hypotheses.claim: Memory poisoning requires query/use-time contextual defenses in addition to write-time provenance/authentication.
hypotheses.prediction: Authenticated but context-triggered or compositionally harmful memories can still redirect candidate formation.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: Strong provenance/integrity checks at write time are sufficient.
hypotheses.falsifier: Adversarial memory benchmark shows no additional protection from query-time role/time/context/utility controls after authenticated writes.

hypotheses.claim: Rich persistent graph state plus a bounded task-conditioned Assembly can outperform maximal-context exposure for a small target model.
hypotheses.prediction: At matched compute/token budget dual-path Assembly improves useful recall/decision quality and reduces context interference.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: Long-context direct exposure eliminates the need for associative graph routing.
hypotheses.falsifier: Target-Qwen benchmark shows maximal-context arm equals/exceeds dual-path on quality, latency, memory and robustness.

hypotheses.claim: Utility adaptation should alter salience/routing only and never silently change canonical claim/status/authority.
hypotheses.prediction: Separating adaptive accessibility from truth allows rollback and prevents reward errors becoming facts.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: Joint truth/salience learning improves adaptation without material integrity risk.
hypotheses.falsifier: A rigorously audited joint learner preserves replay/evidence/authority invariants and materially outperforms separated adaptation.

hypotheses.claim: A novelty/diversity reserve trades some head-topic precision for substantially better rare-topic robustness under long-running salience learning.
hypotheses.prediction: Bounded reserve lowers concentration/HHI and rare-topic failures.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: Diversity reserve wastes scarce Assembly capacity and hurts utility more than it helps.
hypotheses.falsifier: Target traces show reserve has negative net utility across realistic rare-event costs.

hypotheses.claim: Orthogonal semantic/temporal/causal/entity relation views can reduce interference compared with one overloaded relation graph while sharing the same physical store if useful.
hypotheses.prediction: Query-conditioned traversal over typed views improves temporal/causal/role retrieval and reduces irrelevant propagation.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: One typed relation graph plus filters is simpler and equally effective.
hypotheses.falsifier: Matched benchmark shows no accuracy/latency/maintainability advantage after implementation cost.

hypotheses.claim: ClayGraph activation and model-internal workspace uptake are distinct causal stages.
hypotheses.prediction: Changing field/candidate prior can alter availability without corresponding internal-workspace uptake, and vice versa.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: Reader uptake tracks candidate salience closely enough that separate instrumentation adds no value.
hypotheses.falsifier: Target-Qwen nested intervention finds the stages empirically inseparable under controlled projection.
